device.manufacturer: KingSmith Fitness (Beijing KingSmith Technology, Xiaomi ecosystem)
device.name: KingSmith WalkingPad (A1 / R1 / R2 / C2 / X21 / MC21 / Z1 family)
device.notes:
KingSmith's foldable walking pads / under-desk treadmills (WalkingPad A1, A1 Pro, R1, R1 Pro, R2, C2, X21, MC21, Z1 and OEM variants) are controlled over BLE. The manufacturer is alive and shipping new models (kingsmith.com, walkingpad.com, 2026 retail listings), so this is not an abandonment rescue but a cloud-independence spec: the official apps (WalkingPad / com.walkingpad.app, KS Fit / com.kingsmith.xiaojin) tie statistics history, firmware updates and account sync to KingSmith's cloud (JWT login), while every control function is plain local BLE GATT with no pairing, no authentication and no cloud round-trip. Third-party controllers (ph4-walkingpad, QWalkingPad, walkingpad-controller + the hass-walkingpad Home Assistant integration) drive the pads fully offline.
Two protocol generations exist, auto-detected by BLE name and advertised services:
1. Legacy "WiLink" protocol — private service 0xFE00, write 0xFE02,
   notify 0xFE01. Covers A1, A1 Pro, R1 Pro, R2 and early C2 (names like
   "WalkingPad", "KS-R1*"). Frames are 0xF7-prefixed commands and
   0xF8-prefixed responses with a 0xFD terminator; the penultimate byte is
   an additive checksum: cmd[-2] = sum(cmd[1:-2]) & 0xFF. The belt silently
   ignores bad checksums. Speed unit is 0.1 km/h; large counters (time in
   seconds, distance in 10 m units, steps) are 3-byte big-endian integers.
   Confirmed against hardware by ph4-walkingpad (A1) and QWalkingPad
   (A1 Pro).

2. Standard FTMS (Fitness Machine Service 0x1826) — newer models:
   KS-MC21-*, KS-SMC21C-*, ZP-ZEALR1-* (MC-21 family), KS-HD-* (e.g.
   KS-HD-Z1D), X21 generation. Control via the standard Treadmill Control
   Point 0x2AD9 (e.g. SET_TARGET_SPEED = 0x02 + uint16-LE km/h*100, HCI
   snoop-confirmed on MC-21), status via Treadmill Data 0x2ACD. KingSmith
   adds a step counter as bit 13 of the 0x2ACD flags (vendor extension),
   and MC-21-class devices expose a vendor "ODM" characteristic
   d18d2c10-c44c-11e8-a355-529269fb1459 (parent service UUID not captured —
   the official app discovers it by enumeration) that must receive a fixed
   8-byte property-list request (01 00 0d 00 06 0b 0f 0d) before each
   Control Point command; without it the device answers
   CONTROL_NOT_PERMITTED. KS Fit itself tolerates REQUEST_CONTROL being
   rejected and proceeds; implementations should do the same.

Only one BLE central may be connected at a time — if the official app (or the pad's own remote linkage) holds the connection, other clients cannot connect.
SAFETY: this is motorised exercise equipment. Speed/mode/calibration commands move a real belt under a real person; the FTMS and WiLink protocols carry no authentication, so anyone in radio range can start the belt. The child-lock preference exists on WiLink models; treat calibration and max-speed writes as advanced operations.
Cloud dependency: none for control. The apps use KingSmith cloud only for account, workout-history sync and OTA notification. If the cloud dies, local BLE control is unaffected.

credentials.notes: BLE-only control plane; no credentials cross the link and there is no authentication of any kind. Consequence: belt control is open to anyone in range — relevant because the hardware is a moving treadmill.

factory_reset.effect: No factory-reset procedure is documented for any WalkingPad model in the public RE literature or recoverable app strings. The pads hold no network credentials and no bonds, so there is nothing to clear for local control; the preferences block (max speed, child lock, units) is writable over the same unauthenticated BLE channel. Not stated rather than guessed.

methods.description: Connect over GATT. WiLink models: enable notifications on 0xFE01 and write 0xF7-framed commands to 0xFE02. FTMS models: subscribe to 0x2ACD/0x2ADA, write the ODM property-list pre-amble to d18d2c10-… when that characteristic exists, then issue Control Point (0x2AD9) commands.

steps.action: Power on the pad with its physical remote or side switch so it advertises.
Scan for service UUID 0xFE00 (legacy) or 0x1826 (FTMS); match name prefixes WalkingPad / KS- / ZP-ZEALR1 / KINGSMITH / DYNAMAX.
Connect over GATT and discover services; pick WiLink or FTMS flow by what the device exposes.

WiLink: enable notify on 0000fe01, write commands to 0000fe02. FTMS: enable notify/indicate on 0x2ACD/0x2AD9, write the 8-byte ODM pre-amble to d18d2c10-… if present, then write Control Point opcodes to 0x2AD9.
steps.expect: Status notifications arrive (0xF8 0xA2 frames on 0xFE01, or Treadmill Data on 0x2ACD); speed commands change belt speed.

setup.notes: No provisioning, pairing or bonding on either protocol generation: scan for the advertised name ("WalkingPad*" / "KS-*" / "ZP-ZEALR1*") or the service UUIDs 0xFE00 / 0x1826, connect over GATT and send commands. Confidence high: multiple independent open implementations (ph4-walkingpad, QWalkingPad, walkingpad-controller) do exactly this against production hardware. Single-connection limit: only one central at a time.

rejoin.notes: The pad joins no network. Any client may connect once the previous central disconnects (single-connection peripheral).

entities.name: Belt Speed
entities.notes: WiLink models: raw value is 0.1 km/h. FTMS models expose speed in Treadmill Data 0x2ACD instead.

entities.name: Distance
entities.notes: Raw value is 10 m units (171 = 1.71 km).

characteristics.name: Status / record notifications
characteristics.notes: Two response shapes. Current status (header F8 A2, 19 bytes): documented in `format` below; example frame f8 a2 01 0f 01 00 0f d1 00 00 ab 00 12 ae 3c 00 00 00 3a fd = state 1, speed 1.5 km/h, manual mode, time 4049 s, distance 1.71 km, 4782 steps, app-set speed 6.0 km/h (ph4-walkingpad README, decoded against real hardware). Last-workout record (header F8 A7): time at bytes 8..10, distance at 11..13, steps at 14..16 (same 3-byte BE encoding); a second query pops the next stored record. The belt keeps the last record only briefly and loses it on power cut, so final statistics must be fetched promptly after the belt stops.

calibration_mode.advanced_reason: Belt-speed calibration changes how command values map to real belt speed; a miscalibrated pad can run faster than displayed. Recover by re-running calibration on an unloaded belt.
calibration_mode.description: Calibration mode toggle (opcode 0xA2/0x03; QWalkingPad setCali: 1 enables, 0 disables but keeps pad running).

query_last_record.description: Fetch the most recently stored workout record (F8 A7 response); the 0x00 variant pops the next record after the latest has been read.

query_next_record.description: Pop the next stored workout record after query_last_record.

query_params.description: Request the preference block (goal, max/start speed, auto-start, sensitivity, display mask, child lock, units). First of several 10-byte F7 A5 query frames recovered by ph4-walkingpad.

query_status.description: Request current status; pad answers with an F8 A2 frame on 0xFE01.

set_max_speed.advanced_reason: Raises the belt's top speed above the factory walking limit; on foldable pads without handrails a higher ceiling increases fall risk. Recover by writing the factory max back (e.g. 60 = 6.0 km/h on A1).
set_max_speed.description: Convenience form of set_preference with key 3 (0.1 km/h units).

set_preference.description: Write a preference: F7 A6 <key> <subtype> <v2> <v1> <v0> crc FD (value is 3-byte big-endian; subtype 0 except goal type for key 1). Keys: 1 = goal (subtype 0 none / 1 distance / 2 calories / 3 time), 3 = max speed, 4 = start speed, 5 = auto-start on step-on, 6 = sensitivity (1 high / 2 medium / 3 low), 7 = display mask (bit0 time, bit1 speed, bit2 distance, bit3 calories, bit4 steps), 8 = units (0 metric / 1 imperial), 9 = child lock.

set_speed.description: Set belt speed in km/h (wire encoding 0.1 km/h per count, via the parameter's scale); speed 0 stops the belt. 0.5-6.0 km/h usable on A1-class hardware.

start_belt.description: Start the belt (enters run at start speed).

switch_mode.description: Switch belt mode: 0 = automatic (foot-sensing), 1 = manual, 2 = standby.

characteristics.name: Command write
characteristics.notes: All commands are F7-framed with the additive checksum described on the service. Speed unit is 0.1 km/h (30 = 3.0 km/h); usable range on the A1 is 5-60 (0.5-6.0 km/h) and arbitrary 0.1 steps work even where the stock UI only offers 0.5 steps.

services.name: WiLink treadmill service (legacy models)
services.notes: Private KingSmith "WiLink" service on A1/A1 Pro/R1/R2/early-C2 pads. Confirmed in KS Fit v6.5.6 and WalkingPad v2.5.5 app binaries and in the ph4-walkingpad scanner. Frame grammar (both directions): byte 0 = 0xF7 (command, phone->pad) or 0xF8 (response, pad->phone); byte 1 = message class (0xA2 control/status, 0xA5 params, 0xA6 preference write, 0xA7 workout record); final byte = 0xFD; penultimate byte = additive checksum cmd[-2] = sum(cmd[1:-2]) & 0xFF (pad silently ignores bad checksums). 3-byte big-endian integers for time (s), distance (10 m units) and steps. The app polls status roughly every 750 ms; commands should be spaced >= ~700 ms apart (ph4-walkingpad enforces a 0.69 s minimum). Static evidence in com.walkingpad.app v2.5.5 (2026-08-08): the 0xFE00/ FE01/FE02 UUID strings plus dedicated WiLink builder methods (_setSpeed, _setSpeedR1 — an R1-specific speed-command variant — and a _checkSum helper) are present in libapp.so; frames are constructed in code so no constant frames are embedded in the binary. The checksum ALGORITHM is therefore not visible at string level — it rests on the two independent hardware-confirmed implementations (ph4-walkingpad, QWalkingPad), and the R1-specific builder suggests R1 pads may deviate from the A1 frame details (worth one snoop on R1 hardware).

request_control.description: Standard FTMS Request Control. Frequently rejected by KingSmith firmware; ignore the failure and proceed, as KS Fit does.

set_target_speed.description: Standard FTMS Set Target Speed: opcode 0x02 + a single little-endian uint16 speed parameter in 0.01 km/h (raw = km/h * 100; the parser's default endianness is little-endian, matching FTMS). Example: speed 4.0 km/h encodes raw 400 = 0x0190, emitted LE as frame 02 90 01 (HCI-snoop-confirmed on MC-21). Opcode-discrepancy note (resolved 2026-08-08): the "0x03 for speed" claim circulating in walking-pad writeups traces to Ivan Morgillo's Mobvoi Home Walking Pad article — a different vendor/device (TicSports app), not KingSmith. In FTMS 1.0, 0x02 = Set Target Speed and 0x03 = Set Target Inclination; KS Fit v6.5.6 has separate setSpeed and setInclination code paths (string table: WilinkDeviceActionExt|setSpeed / |setInclination, supportInclination), so on incline models (X21) it emits 0x03 for INCLINATION, never for speed. The WalkingPad app v2.5.5 emits no FTMS opcodes at all (WiLink-only binary). KingSmith speed opcode is 0x02 under all known model/firmware conditions.

speed.description: Target belt speed in km/h. min/max bound the RAW wire value (0.01 km/h counts), so 0-2500 = 0-25.0 km/h — well above any walking pad's ceiling; tighten per model from the Supported Speed Range characteristic 0x2AD4 where available.

stop_or_pause.description: Standard FTMS Stop or Pause: parameter 0x01 = stop, 0x02 = pause.

characteristics.name: Treadmill Data
characteristics.notes: Standard FTMS Treadmill Data (flags-gated fields: speed, distance, duration, calories, etc.). KingSmith vendor extension: flag bit 13 adds a step count, per walkingpad-controller.

characteristics.name: Supported Speed Range
characteristics.notes: Standard FTMS; read at connect to learn min/max/step speed.

characteristics.name: Supported Inclination Range
characteristics.notes: Present in the app's characteristic table; relevant on incline-capable models (X21).

characteristics.name: Fitness Machine Status
characteristics.notes: Standard FTMS status events. KS Fit v6.5.6 log strings show a KingSmith-specific 'safe_off' decode of 0x2ADA data ("--> t2ADA: status ", "Received t2ADA data: ", "2ada: device status change: ", "2ADA safe_off list = ", "2ADA safe_off list return"). Interpretation (string-level hypothesis, needs HCI snoop): the app collects the 0x2ADA status events that mean "belt is safely stopped" — per FTMS 1.0 those are opcode 0x03 (Stopped or Paused by the User, param 0x01/0x02) and 0x04 (Stopped by Safety Key), vs 0x02 (Started or Resumed by the User) which clears the state. Exact opcode set and any KingSmith-specific opcodes are not recoverable from the binary's string table — capture on hardware (see capture plan).

initialization.notes: ODM property-list pre-amble. Applies only when the device exposes the vendor characteristic d18d2c10-… (MC-21 class). The parent service UUID is verified ABSENT from both app binaries (full 128-bit-UUID string-table enumeration of KS Fit v6.5.6 and WalkingPad v2.5.5, 2026-08-08: d18d2c10-c44c-11e8-a355-529269fb1459 is the only *-c44c-11e8-* UUID in either app) — the official app binds it purely by GATT enumeration; the parent service UUID must be captured from hardware (see capture plan). KS Fit sends this fixed 8-byte frame before EACH Control Point command, not just once per connection; without it the device returns CONTROL_NOT_PERMITTED to FTMS writes. The response carries the device property table (capabilities, model); walkingpad-controller treats indication-timeout here as success, matching KS Fit.

services.name: Fitness Machine Service (newer models)
services.notes: Standard Bluetooth FTMS on MC-21 / X21 / KS-HD-* generation pads (names KS-MC21-*, KS-SMC21C-*, ZP-ZEALR1-*, KS-HD-*). Characteristic set confirmed in the KS Fit v6.5.6 binary (0x2AD0-0x2ADA strings plus per-opcode log strings); on-wire encodings HCI-snoop-confirmed by mcdax/walkingpad-controller on an MC-21. KingSmith vendor extensions: step counter in Treadmill Data via flag bit 13, and the ODM pre-amble below. KS Fit tolerates REQUEST_CONTROL being rejected and proceeds — replicate that.

characteristics.name: Supplement channel 0b
characteristics.notes: Static-APK-confirmed present and referenced by active code (byte-reversed comparison constant in v6.5.6). Role hypothesis: command/response channel paired with 0d. Properties hypothesized — needs HCI snoop on a KS-HD-* device.

characteristics.name: Supplement channel 0d
characteristics.notes: Static-APK-confirmed present and referenced by active code (byte-reversed comparison constant in v6.5.6). Role hypothesis: command/response channel paired with 0b. Properties hypothesized — needs HCI snoop on a KS-HD-* device.

characteristics.name: Supplement channel 0e
characteristics.notes: Present in the v6.5.6 UUID table only (no active-code reference found). Role unknown — possibly OTA data or long-property channel. Needs HCI snoop.

characteristics.name: Supplement channel 0f
characteristics.notes: Present in the v6.5.6 UUID table only (no active-code reference found). Role unknown — possibly OTA data or long-property channel. Needs HCI snoop.

services.name: KingSmith supplement service (KS-HD-* models)
services.notes: Vendor supplement channel found in KS Fit on KS-HD-* devices (absent on MC-21). KS Fit's FTMSSupplement layer exposes property list, user profile, unit setting, offline workout records, presets/courses and OTA through it; frames use the same body + 1-byte additive checksum wrapping as the ODM channel. Exactly four characteristics exist in the v6.5.6 string table, sharing the 24e2521c-f63b-48ed-85be-c5330XX0fdf7 base: 0b, 0d, 0e, 0f. Static evidence of use (2026-08-08): 0b and 0d also appear in byte-reversed form (f7fd000b-… / f7fd000d-… constants used for UUID comparison in active code paths), while 0e and 0f appear only in the canonical UUID table — so 0b/0d are the live command channels and 0e/0f are discovered table entries (roles TBD). Functional surface from WilinkDeviceSupplementExt symbols in libapp.so: readPropertyList/_parseProperties, _writeSupplementCmd/wrapSupplementCmd (command writes), callBackPropertyStatus/_parseEvent/_parseSupplementCmd (async events + command responses), _parseSystemInfo ("supplement system info: protocolVersion = "), runIdDiffers (offline-record matching) and a full OTA path (startOta/_parseOTA/startModuleOta/ startMcuOta/startMotorOta/installOtaFile/otaSuccess). Exact per-characteristic roles and properties still need an HCI snoop on a KS-HD-* device.

services.name: Device Information Service
services.notes: Standard DIS, in the ph4-walkingpad scan UUID list (model/serial/firmware strings 0x2A24/0x2A25/0x2A26/0x2A28/0x2A29).

services.name: Telink OTA Service
services.notes: Telink OTA service in the ph4-walkingpad scan UUID list (a 0x…2b12 variant also appears) — the pads' BLE SoC is Telink-based and the app delivers firmware updates over it. Flow not documented here; treat OTA writes as bricking risks until captured from a real update.
